The test image shows a pepper fruit with a dark, water-soaked lesion covering the bottom third, with grayish-white mycelium/sporulation at the base. The lesion appears wet and rotted. Top candidates: **Phytophthora_Blight**, **Gray_Mold**, **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**, **Late_Blight**.

Now viewing one reference per candidate:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Pepper fruit with dark, water-soaked, leathery lesion covering the bottom half. Sharp transition from healthy red tissue to dark teal/gray diseased tissue. White sporulation visible at the very base. Classic fruit rot pattern.

- **Phytophthora_Blight ref (Bugwood_21)**: Stem blight on pepper with dark water-soaked lesions and white sporulation — same pathogen (*Phytophthora capsici*), different plant part.

- **Phytophthora_Blight ref (Bugwood_100)**: Field-level view with collapsed pepper plants and rotted fruits on the ground — confirms this disease targets peppers heavily.

- **Gray_Mold ref (Bugwood_13)**: Tomato fruit with gray fuzzy growth in cracks at blossom end — doesn't match (no visible Botrytis gray fuzz in test image, different lesion character).

- **Rhizopus ref (Bugwood_1)**: Microscopic view of black sporangia — completely different.

The test image shows a pepper fruit with a dark, water-soaked, leathery lesion with white sporulation at the base — this is the hallmark of **Phytophthora capsici fruit rot**, which falls under Phytophthora_Blight.
